briefs.title: the divergence is the story
briefs.flows: SOL sits near $76, mid-range in the $74–78 band it has held all week. spot DEX volume printed $1.45b over 24 hours, on a week tracking down ~8%. perps matched it at $1.43b. quiet tape, two-sided.
briefs.launches: pump is still the largest venue on the chain — $335m in 24 hours, roughly 23% of all DEX volume, ahead of bisonfi ($216m) and humidifi ($161m). the flow is concentrated in the venue, not in any single new name: nothing that launched this week is holding a top volume slot.
briefs.wallets: ETF desks turned buyers — $8.8m net inflow, the strongest day since may 12, after months of near-zero. separately, ~$17m of SOL has walked off an exchange hot wallet into one fresh address over the past week with no re-deposit observed. exchange-out with no round trip reads as positioning, not distribution.

watching.text: u.s. Solana ETF flows, after the strongest inflow day since spring
watching.expectation: at least one more day of net inflows within the next two sessions

briefs.read: the divergence is the story. price has spent a week inside a $4 band while the usage side keeps grinding: ~2m daily active addresses, $500b in stablecoin transfer volume last month, and a network upgrade landing next week that cuts state rent ~90%. flat price against rising throughput resolves eventually — in which direction is not rigel's job to guess, only to log which side blinks first. today, the first ETF bid since spring blinked.

calls.call: u.s. Solana ETF products log at least one more day of net inflows within the next two sessions

board.s: price has held the $74–78 band for a week while daily active addresses (~2m), stablecoin transfer volume ($500b in july), and DEX throughput grind higher. divergences like this eventually resolve; rigel tracks which side moves first.
board.invalidation: a daily close below $74 with DEX volume fading under $1.2b — that would say the usage story isn't pricing in.
